steps.title: The tilted Earth
steps.say: The Earth orbits the Sun, and its axis is tilted 23.5° and always points the same way in space.

steps.title: Northern winter
steps.say: In December the northern half leans away from the Sun, so sunlight arrives at a low angle and is spread out, and days are short. The Sun is overhead in the south.

steps.title: Spring equinox
steps.say: A quarter of a year later, neither half leans toward the Sun. It is overhead at the equator, and days and nights are about equal.

steps.title: Northern summer
steps.say: In June the northern half leans toward the Sun. Light hits more directly and days are long, so it is warmer. The Sun is overhead in the north.

steps.title: Autumn equinox
steps.say: Then the Earth reaches the other equinox, with balanced light again, and the north cools toward winter.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.say: Seasons come from the tilt, not from distance to the Sun. Drag the Earth to where it is summer in the south.
